outcome: The general Greenberg invariants conjecture (μ = λ = 0 for the cyclotomic Zp-extension of any totally real number field) and Greenberg's p-rationality conjecture remain open; work since 26 January 2024 consists of case verifications, analogues, and bound improvements on related-but-distinct problems, none of which settle a case of the stated conjectures.
summary: Greenberg's conjectures (the invariants conjecture that μ_p(k) = λ_p(k) = 0 for the cyclotomic Zp-extension of any totally real number field k and every prime p, and the later p-rationality conjecture) remain open as of September 2026. The Wikipedia article on 'Greenberg's conjecture' still states both are unsolved and reports no update beyond the Ferrero–Washington theorem (1979, predates the window) and other pre-2024 background. Searching the recent arXiv literature turns up an active stream of work adjacent to the conjecture but none of it is a case of the stated conjecture itself: (1) arXiv:2410.05706 (Oct 2024) proves an *analogue* of Greenberg's conjecture for CM fields — a different (though related) problem posed over different objects, not a restriction of the totally-real-field statement; (2) arXiv:2503.00819 (Mar 2025) and arXiv:2503.15727 (Mar 2025) extend computational/numerical verification of the conjecture to larger discriminant ranges for real quadratic and real biquadratic fields respectively — this narrows where a counterexample could hide but does not settle any case, consistent with §3.1's rule that record-extension for an existence-type statement does not count as movement (and here the object itself, μ=λ=0, is not even a record but a repeated finite check); (3) other results found (arXiv:2405.05871, arXiv:2408.07826) address a differently-worded 'Greenberg conjecture for elliptic curve Selmer groups' (μ-invariant of Selmer groups of elliptic curves over Q), which is a namesake variant, not the totally-real-field invariants conjecture, and even there the results are bounds (μ ≤ 1) on a still-open statement rather than resolutions. No source anywhere in this search mentions AI, machine learning, or a large language model contributing to any of this work — all located papers describe conventional analytic/algebraic number theory arguments and computer algebra class-group computations (not AI systems). Given the consistent picture across the Wikipedia article, general searches, and inspection of the specific recent papers turned up, and agreement with the triage pass's conclusion, confidence is high that nothing has happened to the stated conjectures in the window and that no AI system was involved in any adjacent work.
competing_reading: One could argue the CM-field analogue (arXiv:2410.05706) or the elliptic-curve Selmer-group 'Greenberg conjecture' results are close enough in spirit to count as progress on 'Greenberg's conjectures' broadly construed, since Wikipedia's bullet is terse and doesn't pin down which of Greenberg's several conjectures it means beyond the invariants conjecture. But by §3.1's test — does this change what a careful person would write in this bullet's entry, which concerns totally real fields — these are variants over different objects (CM fields; elliptic curve Selmer groups) rather than restrictions of the totally-real-field statement, so they do not count as movement on the stated problem.
what_would_settle_it: A proof or disproof of μ_p(k) = λ_p(k) = 0 for some specific totally real field k and prime p not already known (or a general proof), or explicit resolution of the p-rationality conjecture for some field/prime, reported by a source dated after 26 January 2024.
